methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $130M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 1 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

private.name: SambaNova Systems
private.rationale: Same sector (Chips & Semiconductors), same stage (Series A), post-money $11B

data.narrative:
SiPearl is a Series A-stage semiconductor company founded by Philippe Notton that has raised €130M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is reliably applicable. This approach uses the company's €130M in total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the next financing stage, yielding an implied valuation of €260M. The public-comp anchoring method cannot be deployed because SiPearl's revenue is not disclosed, which is standard for private-stage companies. A narrow peer-median approach also proves inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or similar-tier private comparables meeting the minimum threshold of three datapoints.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €221M to €299M, with a median of €260M. This range reflects reasonable upside and downside variance around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue visibility for revenue-multiple anchoring, limited granularity in the private peer set for direct median comparison, and the inherent variance in stage-advancement multiers across market conditions and investor appetite within semiconductor financing.
